title: EASE – EEG in Acute Sepsis-Associated Encephalopathy: An Exploratory Prospective Observational Study of Early EEG Dynamics
summary:
epsis can impair not only peripheral organs but also brain function. This condition, referred to as sepsis-associated encephalopathy, may present with confusion, delirium, reduced alertness or, in severe cases, coma. Currently, there is no simple objective method for routinely assessing these early changes in brain function in intensive care patients.
This observational study investigates whether changes in electrical brain activity measured by electroencephalography (EEG) are associated with the severity of sepsis and related organ dysfunction. Sixty adult patients with sepsis will undergo three short EEG recordings within 24 hours. Routinely collected clinical data and neurological assessments will be analyzed in parallel. In addition, a single blood sample will be obtained to explore possible associations between EEG alterations and changes in the immune system.
The study does not alter the patients' medical treatment. Its aim is to improve the understanding of early EEG alterations during sepsis and to provide a basis for future methods for the objective detection and monitoring of sepsis-associated brain dysfunction.

interventions.name: Adult intensive care patients with sepsis according to Sepsis-3 criteria. Three standardized 10-minute frontal EEG recordings are performed within 24 hours after study inclusion. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years
Treatment in the intensive care unit
Sepsis according to the sepsis 3 criteria
Exclusion criteria:
Minority
Technically not feasible frontal EEG derivation (e.g. Lack of access to the forehead due to bandages or wounds)
Acute neurosurgical intervention or neurological diseases with relevant influence on the EEG (e.g. epilepsy, hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy, advanced neurodegenerative diseases)
Suspected CNS infection
Pregnancy
